The image shows three visible shelves packed with various books, primarily manga or graphic novels given the spine art and text styles. The lighting is somewhat dim, casting shadows within the shelf compartments. The perspective is from the left side, looking towards the right corner of the room.

artifact_observations.location: Book spines on all visible shelves
artifact_observations.reasoning: The text on the book spines is largely illegible or nonsensical. While some characters resemble Japanese Kanji or Katakana, many are malformed, fused, or dissolve into texture noise upon close inspection. This is a common AI artifact where text simulation fails at the character level.

The spines lack realistic physical depth and separation. Some books appear to fuse into one another, and the edges of the pages (fore-edge) are often blurred or indistinguishable from the spine color, lacking the typical texture of paper layers.

The items on the bottom shelf, particularly the white box-like object on the right, have ambiguous geometry. It is unclear if it is a box, a stack of papers, or part of the shelf structure, suggesting slight structural ambiguity or melting.

focus_areas: Legibility and structure of text on book spines
Physical separation and boundary definition between individual books
Geometric consistency of shelf alignment and perspective
Realism of book spine textures and page edges
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the 'text_gibberish' artifact. In real photos, even blurry text usually maintains consistent character spacing and baseline alignment. AI often generates 'text-like' textures that fail OCR or show impossible character shapes. Also, verify if the 'fusion' of books is a result of low resolution or actual generative failure. The classifier should easily identify 'bookcase', but the text auditor is the critical discriminator for authenticity here.
